title: Reproducing Johnson, Biegelsen and Moyer 1981: interface states and the Pb centre removed by low-temperature anneals and atomic deuterium

sample.paper: “The substrates were boron doped for p-type conductivity.” “(111)-oriented single-crystal silicon”
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si111; DOPING: p_type_boron (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.paper: “MOS capacitors fabricated on p-type epitaxial silicon, with degenerately doped (p+) substrates”
sample.ours: SUBSTRATE: p_epi_on_p_plus (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: Epitaxial layer thickness and doping not stated.

sample.paper: “For ESR measurements both surfaces of (111)-oriented silicon wafers were polished and oxidized.”
sample.note: ESR counts both faces; the paper's spin density is per cm² of interface, presumably halved.

sample.paper: 116 nm (Fig. 1), 2000 Å (Fig. 2), 94 nm (Figs 5, 6), 219 nm (Fig. 4); dry O2 at 1000 °C, no post-oxidation anneal
sample.ours: the 1965 growth law from bare silicon, time chosen for the thickness

sample.paper: aluminium, rf-induction evaporation, 1000 Å on the ESR wafers
sample.note: No program reads a metal film or the hydrogen it releases.

history.item: Dry oxidation at 1000 °C to 116 nm, no post-oxidation anneal
history.paper: “Silicon-dioxide thin films were grown on (111)-oriented single-crystal silicon by furnace oxidation in dry O2 at 1000°C.” Fig. 1: “116 nm SiO2”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 8400 TEMP 1000->1000 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Temperature and gas are stated; the time is not. Ours is the time the predictor's 1965 growth law needs for 116 nm at 1000 °C (2.3 h); the alignment searches it against the thickness.

history.item: Rapid cool to room temperature in the furnace gas
history.paper: “The oxides did not receive a high-temperature postoxidation anneal and were rapidly cooled to room temperature in the furnace ambient.”
history.ours: RUN Cool DURATION 600 TEMP 1000->25 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: “Rapidly” and “in the furnace ambient” are the paper's; the 10 min straight fall to 25 °C is ours.

history.paper: “Capacitors with the MOS structure were formed by vacuum evaporating aluminum with an rf-induction heated source. This evaporation source does not introduce radiation damage in the SiO2 layer”
history.ours: not in our history: no program reads a metal film
history.note: Aluminium matters to this paper as a hydrogen source (the sinter releases hydrogen, p. 1); the language cannot say that, see the variant.

history.item: Current-transient DLTS, hole emission, σp = 5×10⁻¹⁴ cm² assumed
history.paper: “the analysis assumed the value of 5 X 10^-14 cm2 for the hole capture cross section”; “Near the silicon midgap the DLTS measurement is influenced by minority-carrier … processes”
history.ours: the observables Dit and Dit at 0.30 eV
history.note: The paper marks the curves near midgap as unreliable (dashed above about 0.62 eV).

history.paper: Fig. 2: “Vacuum Anneals (15 min)” at 30 to 600 °C, with Al, without Al, and after atomic D
history.ours: one history per temperature, a single anneal each
history.note: Whether one specimen was annealed in sequence is not stated; in sequence the time at temperature would add up.

history.paper: Figs 3-6: 94 and 219 nm oxides, deuteration at 25, 100, 230 °C for 30 min; post-deuteration vacuum anneals 15 min to 600 °C
history.note: No program has a hydrogen or deuterium concentration in the oxide.

history.paper: “no accumulation was detected in oxides annealed under identical conditions in molecular deuterium”
history.note: Only SIMS; the spin density after molecular D2 is not given.

cases.label: ESR wafer, atomic deuterium at 230 °C, then vacuum 600 °C 15 min
cases.note: Not scored: the paper's value is zero (no spin signal after any vacuum anneal up to 600 °C), which a relative tolerance cannot score. Brower's dissociation rate (Ed 2.56 eV, 1.2×10¹² s⁻¹, as cited by Stesmans 1996) gives 83% of the sites back after 15 min at 600 °C; the paper sees none.
